+---
+`builtin/validators/code-hygiene/rules/missing-docs-rust.md` runs `cargo clippy --message-format=json --quiet -- -W missing_docs` and declares `supersedes: [missing-docs]`.
+
+`missing-docs.md` exempts "Generated code". Its two Rust siblings, `complexity-rust` and `dead-code-rust`, both carry `select(.file | startswith("/") | not)` in their `jq` filter to drop cargo's `OUT_DIR` output. This rule's filter carries no such step, so generated code under `OUT_DIR` that declares public items is reported with an absolute path, at a file the author cannot edit.
+
+A second inconsistency in the same command, in the losing direction: the command omits `--workspace` and `sort -u`, which both siblings carry. Plain `cargo clippy` lints only the current package, so in a multi-crate workspace this rule under-reports although its declared `scope` is `workspace`.
+
+Four carve-outs ARE reproduced, all by rustc: private items; tests, because the command omits `--all-targets` and a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` is private anyway; obvious implementations, because `missing_docs` does not require docs on trait `impl` items; and `#[doc(hidden)]`.
+
+Decide both: the `OUT_DIR` filter, and whether the command takes `--workspace`.
+
+Found by the `supersedes` survey on ^h7garpc. #tool-validators #objectivity

So the under-report is a member no package depends on, and not every member. This repository is a VIRTUAL workspace root, where cargo selects every member already, so `--workspace` changes nothing here: 1262 lines either way.
+
+**CORRECTED — the `OUT_DIR` finding does NOT reach the author today.** The script reports it, and the ENGINE drops it. `run_tool_script` keeps, for a `workspace`-scope run, only the findings whose normalized path stands in the run's matched files, and an `OUT_DIR` path normalizes to `target/debug/build/.../out/generated.rs`, which no changed file matches. Measured on a probe crate whose build script writes one undocumented `pub struct` and one undocumented `pub fn` into `OUT_DIR`: the script without the step names 3 findings, two of them at an absolute path under `target/`; the script with the step names the one hand-written item. The step is still added, for the reason the rule body now states: it makes the SCRIPT's own answer equal the rule's answer, and it makes the three Rust rules alike.
+
+**CONFIRMED — `sort -u` is load-bearing.** Cargo compiles a package one time for each way the workspace uses it. Measured on the probe workspace, where `shared` is a dependency and a build-dependency of the root package: `shared/src/lib.rs:3` arrives two times. Measured on this workspace: 1262 lines, 1179 unique; the 83 lines removed repeat 77 findings in 18 files.
+
+**CONFIRMED — the four carve-outs.** One probe crate holding each shape reports 2 findings, and both are the getter and the setter of the section below. Silent: `struct PrivateStruct`, `fn private_function`, a `pub struct` and a `pub fn` inside a private `mod`; a `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` holding `pub struct TestHelperType`, `pub fn test_helper` and a `#[test] fn`; `impl fmt::Display for Shown` and `impl Default for Shown`; `#[doc(hidden)] pub struct Hidden` and `#[doc(hidden)] pub fn hidden_function`.
+
+**CONFIRMED — `--all-targets` is load-bearing for a test target.** A probe crate holding `tests/it.rs` with an undocumented `pub struct IntegrationHelper` stays silent under the shipped command and reports under `--all-targets`. The command keeps no `--all-targets`.
+
+**FOUND — the run answered 0 for a crate that does not compile.** `cargo clippy` exits 101 for such a crate and writes no `missing_docs` diagnostic. The earlier pipe ended in `jq`, so the pipeline exited 0 with no output, which reads as a clean crate. `builtin/validators/README.md` states the requirement under the `run` key. The script now writes cargo's report to a file, and `set -e` makes cargo's exit status the exit status of the script. Card ^y4xyw1g carries the same defect in `complexity-rust`, `dead-code-rust` and `unused-dependencies-rust`.
